chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraj, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him); and by different chains, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed us in his house, or he said, in the palace, while we were gathered. Then he (peace be upon him) ordered, so it was written in a letter and read out to the people. And others have reported that Ibn al-Kawa asked the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) about the description of Islam, Faith, Disbelief, and Hypocrisy.

He said: As for after (praising Allah), indeed Allah, Blessed and High, legislated Islam and made its laws easy for the one who embraced it, and strengthened its pillars against the one who opposed it, and made it a honor for the one who loved it, and a security for the one who entered it, and a guidance for the one who aspired to it, and an adornment for the one who glorified it, and a pardon for the one who desired it, and a handle for the one who held fast to it, and a rope for the one who attached himself to it, and a proof for the one who spoke by it, and a light for the one who illuminated with it, and an aid for the one who sought assistance with it.

And a witness for the one who contends with it, and a success for the one who argues by it, and a knowledge for the one who imbibes it, and a Hadith for the one who reports it, and a ruling for the one who judges, and a forbearance for the one who experiments, and an apparel for the one who manages, and an understanding for the one who discerns, and a conviction for the one who minds, and an insight for the one who determines, and a sign for the one who labels, and a lesson for the one who pays attention, and a salvation for the one who is truthful, and a discipline for the one who is righteous, and a nearness for the one who approaches, and a reliability for the one who relies, and a prosperity for the one who delegates.

And an advancement for the one who is good, and a goodness for the one who is eager, and a shield for the one who is patient, and a clothing for the one who is pious, and a backer for the one who is guided, and a cave for the one who believes, and an entrustment for the one who submits, and a hope for the one who ratifies, and sufficiency for the one who is content.

So that is the Truth. Its way is Guidance, its narration is Glory, and its description is the Best. It is the brightest of the manifestos, the shining of the minarets, the purest of the lanterns, raised to the peak. Its track is easy to race upon, gathering the arena, swift in the advance, painful in the retribution, complete in preparation, noble in the horses.

So Faith is its manifesto, and the righteous deeds are its minarets, and understanding (Fiqh) are its lamps, and the world is its race track, and death is its peak, and the Resurrection is its arena, and Paradise is its advance, and the Fire is its retribution, and Piety is its preparation, and the doers of good are its horses.

So by Faith, one is guided to the righteous deeds, and by the righteous deeds, Fiqh is established, and by Fiqh, Death is feared, and by Death, the world is concluded, and by the Resurrection, Paradise is approached, and Paradise is the regret of the people of the Fire, and the Fire is the admonition of the pious, and Piety is the root of Faith.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and practical benefits of Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, often cited as the 'Description of Islam' (Sifat al-Islam), is attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) but is frequently discussed in Shia scholarship in the context of Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) sermon in the mosque of Kufa, highlighting the ontological status of Islam as a divine reality before its legal codification. It emphasizes that Islam is not merely a set of rituals but a comprehensive epistemological and spiritual framework where Faith (Iman) serves as the foundation, Piety (Taqwa) as its core essence, and Good Deeds as its manifestation, ultimately leading to the ultimate success of Paradise.
